key_insight: PAW turns a natural-language function specification into a compact neural artifact that can be executed locally and reused cheaply, instead of calling a large model for every input.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical path to offline, low-latency, and lower-memory deployment for fuzzy tasks like log filtering, JSON repair, and intent ranking.
method: Train a 4B compiler on FuzzyBench to translate specs into parameter-efficient adapters.
Use a frozen 0.6B Qwen3 interpreter to execute the generated PAW programs.
Compile once per function definition, then reuse the artifact for many low-cost calls.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a 10M-example dataset and that a 0.6B Qwen3 interpreter running PAW matches direct prompting of Qwen3-32B while using about 1/50 the inference memory and reaching 30 tokens/s on a MacBook M3.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the compiler-generated adapter and the frozen interpreter, so robustness on out-of-distribution fuzzy functions may be a practical concern.
paper_title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
